title: Build a reading den
description: Blankets over chairs, cushions on the floor, a pile of favourite books — a reading den is a tiny fort where stories feel even better. Build one and move in with a book.

body.heading: Build your den
paragraphs: Choose two or three chairs and stand them back to back with a gap between them. Drape a big blanket or bedsheet over the tops so it makes a roof. If the roof sags, a grown-up can help you clip the edges with clothes pegs.
Now make it cosy: cushions or pillows on the floor, a soft blanket to sit on, and maybe one cuddly toy as a reading buddy. Leave a doorway gap so you can climb in and out easily.

body.heading: Move in with books
paragraphs: Pick three books — one favourite you know by heart, one you have never read, and one full of pictures. Carry them into your den like treasure.

Read lying down, sitting up, or whispering the story to your reading buddy. A den makes even a book you have read ten times feel like a brand-new adventure. When you finish, swap one book for a new one and dive back in.

takeaway: Drape a blanket over chairs, fill the den with cushions, and take three books inside — a fort makes every story feel bigger.
ageGuidance: Ages 3–8, with a grown-up helping to build.
materials: Clothes pegs to clip the roof (optional)
supervision: A grown-up helps build the den, checks it is sturdy, and stays nearby while the child plays and reads in it.
safetyNotes: Build on a flat floor away from heaters, candles and stairs, and never use heavy objects to hold the roof down.
Leave a wide doorway gap and make sure the child can get out easily at all times — dens are for reading, never for sleeping in overnight.
screenFreeExtension: Take your three books outside on a dry day and read them under a tree instead — a den made by nature.
